summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, and shortness of breath. She was found to have severe hyponatremia (Na 119) due to poor oral intake on a 'tea and toast' diet, exacerbated by gastroparesis and missed peritoneal dialysis. Her sodium improved with fluid restriction, solute supplementation, and daily manual dialysis. Constipation was severe despite a home bowel regimen; a CT scan showed significant stool burden. She responded well to soap suds enemas, which were taught for home use. Peritoneal fluid studies showed no infection. She was stabilized, discharged on her baseline medications, with instructions to resume her PD cycler, continue enemas, maintain fluid restriction, and follow up with nephrology and GI.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
